tools.name: attach_codesys
tools.description: Take over a CODESYS the user opened by hand (the MCP did not start it, so it has no watcher), e.g. to work in the project the user has open. Writes the attach script and waits for the user to run it once in that CODESYS: Tools > Scripting > Execute Script File..., pick the script (path in the reply). The script installs the MCP watcher and returns; CODESYS stays fully usable. Then every tool for that install runs in that CODESYS. The MCP never closes or kills an attached CODESYS: shutdown_codesys (and the server stopping with --no-keep-alive) only detaches; with the default keep-alive the next session takes it over. Opening another project never closes one with unsaved changes (close_project saveFirst=false still does, as asked). Tell the user the menu path and the script path BEFORE calling with a long waitSeconds, or call with waitSeconds 0 first to get the path.

install.description: Only attach a CODESYS of this install (SP22 Patch 1). Default: whichever CODESYS runs the script.

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the script to be run. Default 180. 0: only write the script and report its path (and attach at once if it already ran).

killExisting.description: If true, kill orphans of the install before launching: CODESYS an ended MCP session started that no live session uses. Never one opened by hand, attached or not, nor another live session's; other installs are unaffected. One with unsaved changes is not killed: the call asks first (answer with otherInstances).

otherInstances.description: The USER's answer when a launch asked what to do with other CODESYS of the install that cannot be taken over (never answer it yourself): 'leave' starts a new CODESYS next to them (remembered for this session), 'close' closes them like the window's X (CODESYS asks about unsaved changes itself), 'save-and-close' saves their unsaved projects where the MCP can reach them, then closes them. Another live session's CODESYS is always left alone.

tools.name: create_redundancy_config
tools.description: Adds the 'Redundancy Configuration' object to an application (or updates the existing one) and configures it without the GUI editor: redundancy link IPs/ports (1st and optional 2nd link), redundancy task, timeouts, auto sync, debug messages, sync-time trace, and which GVLs/POUs are excluded from synchronization (Registered Areas). Always creates the hidden PLC2 device object the editor normally creates on first open when it is missing (a missing one makes every compile pop 'The object GUID ... is not valid'). Optional online steps for the PLC2 path (both fail loudly if no address ends up bound; PLC1 is the application's own device, set it with rebind_device_to_scan_result): plc2Address binds PLC2 to an address and is the only option that works for a PLC a UDP scan cannot see, such as an SSH-tunnelled one (live-proven); plc2Gateway + plc2DeviceName instead runs the editor's 'Set Path PLC2' batch command, which matches a gateway scan result by name (only its failure path has been exercised so far). writeSettings=true first connects to both PLCs, then runs the editor's 'Write' batch command, which pushes the settings to BOTH PLCs and assigns PlcIdent 1/2; they apply after a runtime restart. On WAGO PFC200 FW31 they land in /home/codesys_root/CODESYSControl.cfg ([CmpRedundancyConnectionIP] + [CmpRedundancy]), not in the eRUNTIME.cfg of WAGO's older how-to. writeSettings requires the PLC2 path. For the online steps pass deviceUser+devicePassword; do not ask the user to fill in a login. A Write failure after the reachability check is shown as an error message box. OPEN BUG (2026-10-01): plc2Address through an SSH tunnel failed with 'SetActivePath failed for 127.0.0.1:11746 via gateway Gateway-1: None'; the PLC2 path is not needed when both PLCs already hold the settings, because PLC2 receives the boot application from PLC1. Only the fields you pass are changed. Saves the project. Needs the CODESYS Redundancy add-on in the IDE profile. KNOWN GAP: unlike the GUI editor, the tool does not populate the object's internal CyclicUpdate list (the editor's per-object 'update cyclic' flag), so a tool-made configuration has no cyclically-updated areas; set them in the editor if the application needs them.

tools.name: bump_project_version
tools.description: Bumps one part of the 4-part Project Information.Version field of the primary project (Major.Minor.Revision.Build) and saves the project. Also maintains a `_MCP_PROJECT_VERSION` GVL under Application with the new version as `sVersion : STRING := '<X.Y.Z.W>'` so the running PLC carries the version at a known address (read it via the read_running_version_online tool). The GVL is created on first bump and updated in place thereafter. Convention: major = incompatible API break (rename FB / change public signature / remove method); minor = backward-compatible feature add (new FB / GVL / method); revision = bug fix only; build = internal counter, often 0 for hand-released versions. Bumping a higher part resets all lower parts to 0. FIRST-RUN: if no version is set yet (None/empty/0.0.0.0), seeds at 1.0.0.0 regardless of level so a first-time bump gives a canonical starting point instead of 0.0.0.1. AUTO MODE: if level='auto', the tool diffs the project's mcp-mirror/ folder against the latest v* git tag and classifies the change (deletion/rename -> major; addition -> minor; modification -> revision; no changes -> short-circuits with no bump; first-run -> seed at 1.0.0.0).

tools.name: release_project_version
tools.description: ONE-SHOT release pipeline. Runs the full sync from a CODESYS code change all the way to a tagged + pushed git commit, with no manual orchestration in between. Sequence: (1) mirror_export refreshes mcp-mirror/; (2) classifier diffs the new mirror against the latest v* tag; (3) if no changes, short-circuits with 'no version change'; (4) otherwise bump_project_version with the resolved level; (5) regenerate library.md as markdown; (6) regenerate pou-dump.md as markdown; (7) regex-replace the version reference in README.md; (8) Changelog.md auto-appended with the new entry (timestamp + classification evidence); (9) git add the controlled paths only (mcp-mirror, the four .md files, .gitignore, the .project binary); (10) git commit; (11) git tag v<new>; (12) git push --follow-tags. Standard workflow: ask Claude to run release_project_version after every confirmed change in CODESYS. Requires the project's parent dir to be a git repo with a configured remote.

tools.name: read_running_version_ssh
tools.description: Reads the running project version from a CODESYS Control Linux PLC via SSH, by extracting the X.Y.Z.W literal of `_MCP_PROJECT_VERSION.sVersion` from the boot application binary. Bypasses CODESYS entirely - no IDE running, no project lock, no online protocol. The boot app is fetched with `cat` and its strings are picked by the MCP, so the PLC needs no `strings` (WAGO BusyBox has none). Requires SSH key auth (one-time setup, see the error message if you don't have it); the host may be an ~/.ssh/config alias, so a ProxyJump route works (e.g. 'plc-b', user 'root'). As root no sudo is used, else passwordless sudo for `cat`. Linux PLCs only (CODESYS Control on Raspberry Pi, IPC, WAGO PFC200/CC100, etc.). Several X.Y.Z.W literals (library versions) and no unique one means the project has no _MCP_PROJECT_VERSION: they are listed as candidates.

tools.name: restart_runtime_ssh
tools.description: Restart the CODESYS Control runtime on a Linux PLC via SSH, then poll the runtime's listen port (default 11740, via `ss` or `netstat`) until it comes up - the real liveness signal, since `systemctl is-active` reports 'active' even after the runtime died from licence-demo expiry. Restarts the systemd unit `service` if systemd knows it, else `/etc/init.d/<service>` stop+start, else (default service only) WAGO's `/etc/init.d/runtime` stop+start, so it also works on WAGO PFC200/CC100. Auth: with a password (or the default host codesys-pi.local / karstein / codesys123) it uses password auth and feeds sudo via `sudo -S`; for any other host given without a password it uses key auth through the system ssh, so an ~/.ssh/config alias with ProxyJump works (e.g. host 'plc-a', user 'root' for PLCs behind a jump host). As root no sudo is used. A restart stops the running PLC application: make sure nobody else is working on that PLC first.
